# Mirror contacts across systems: Gmail

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers contact-sync work end to end across Gmail, Google Sheets and HubSpot.

It moves through 14 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes (Gmail)
4. Normalize Records
5. Upsert into HubSpot
6. Advance Watermark
7. Persist Watermark (Google Sheets)
8. Tag Pipeline Metadata
9. Guard Non-Empty email
10. Stamp Processing Time
11. Align Field Names
12. Summarize Run Stats
13. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
14. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing contact-sync work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes (Gmail) → Normalize Records → Upsert into HubSpot → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (Google Sheets) → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Guard Non-Empty email → Stamp Processing Time → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Gmail and Google Sheets aligned by hand for contact sync
- Contact sync work where "Fetch Changes (Gmail)" is still a manual step before Gmail
- Contact sync work that only reaches Gmail on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Gmail and Google Sheets in step for contact sync, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Gmail or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 16 nodes in this contact-sync build
- Fans the same result out to HubSpot in the same run, for contact sync
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 16 nodes for contact sync before wiring Gmail
- 16 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for contact sync

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your contact sync process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.

**Do not log**
contact-sync payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
